record.original_question: For a finite semigroup S, define its group complexity to be the smallest integer n such that S divides a finite alternating wreath product A0 ◦ G1 ◦ A1 ◦ ··· ◦ Gn ◦ An with each Ai aperiodic and each Gi a group. Is there an algorithm that computes the group complexity of a semigroup from its multiplication table?

evidence.quote: The group complexity of S is the smallest possible integer n over all decompositions of type (∗).
Problem 6 Is there an algorithm to compute the group complexity of a semigroup, given its multiplication table?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a finite semigroup. Recall that a semigroup is called aperiodic if all of its subgroups are trivial, and that $T$ divides $U$ means $T$ is a homomorphic image of a subsemigroup of $U$. The wreath product $\circ$ of finite semigroups (or transformation semigroups) is the standard one used in Krohn–Rhodes theory. By the Krohn–Rhodes decomposition theorem, every finite semigroup $S$ divides an alternating wreath product
$$A_0 \circ G_1 \circ A_1 \circ G_2 \circ \cdots \circ G_n \circ A_n,$$
where each $A_i$ is a finite aperiodic semigroup and each $G_i$ is a finite group. Define the group complexity $c(S)$ of $S$ to be the smallest nonnegative integer $n$ for which such a decomposition exists.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input the multiplication table of a finite semigroup $S$, computes the group complexity $c(S)$?
artifact.category_tag: Krohn-Rhodes group complexity of finite semigroups
artifact.status_search_result: The decidability of Krohn–Rhodes group complexity is a long-standing open problem (over 50 years). Decidability of complexity $c=1$ was established by Henckell–Rhodes–Steinberg, and in June 2024 Margolis, Rhodes, and Schilling posted a preprint claiming decidability for all $k$ (arXiv:2406.18477). The general result has not yet been fully confirmed by the community as of 2026, so the problem is best described as partially solved / claim awaiting verification.

status_evidence.title: Decidability of Krohn-Rhodes complexity for all finite semigroups and automata
status_evidence.snippet: Main result proves it is decidable whether a finite semigroup has complexity k for any k ≥ 0.
status_evidence.claim: Claimed proof (2024) that group complexity is decidable in general; awaiting community verification.

status_evidence.title: Decidability of Krohn-Rhodes complexity c = 1 of finite semigroups and automata
status_evidence.snippet: Proves decidability of Krohn-Rhodes complexity c = 1.
status_evidence.claim: Case n = 1 of group complexity is decidable.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of Finite Semigroups: History and Decidability
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the history and recent decidability results for Krohn-Rhodes complexity.
status_evidence.claim: The decidability problem has been open for more than 50 years; recent work claims a resolution.
